facts.claim: The U.S. Department of Commerce awarded Texas Instruments up to $1.61 billion in CHIPS direct funding supporting more than $18 billion of planned investment through the end of the decade across three new Texas/Utah facilities, independently corroborating the scale and policy support behind TXN's U.S. 300mm capacity expansion.

Reuters reported Q2 2026 revenue of $5.46 billion, up 23% year over year and above consensus, with broad growth led by industrial, data center and automotive; it also reported Q3 revenue guidance of $5.65-$6.15 billion above the cited $5.61 billion analyst estimate.

risks.risk: Government support validates strategic importance and financing support but does not establish utilization or return on incremental fab capital; underutilization remains an underwriting risk.
Strong current demand and above-consensus guidance do not eliminate semiconductor cyclicality or guarantee sustained industrial/automotive recovery.

unknowns.unknown: Current peer-relative valuation, incremental 300mm utilization and realized return on new capacity remain for Council Alpha underwriting.
